title: Check your understanding: Repository Access and Permissions

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of repository access and permissions?
options: Repository access permissions are commonly enforced by the hosting service, not by the local Git object database. Separate read access, write access, branch protection, approvals and credential scope.
Git automatically backs up every file, including ignored and untracked files, to a remote.
The operation grants every contributor write access to the hosted repository.
questions.answer_key: Repository access permissions are commonly enforced by the hosting service, not by the local Git object database. Separate read access, write access, branch protection, approvals and credential scope.
questions.explanation: Repository access permissions are commonly enforced by the hosting service, not by the local Git object database. Separate read access, write access, branch protection, approvals and credential scope.

questions.prompt: Which command is the most direct starting point for this lesson’s example?
questions.explanation: Use `git ls-remote origin` as the first inspection/action in the example, and then verify the result with the companion checks in the lesson.

questions.prompt: Which is the safest general practice when working with repository access and permissions?
options: Inspect the repository state, verify the expected result, and protect valuable work before destructive or history-changing operations.
Run the most destructive option first; the reflog guarantees every file can always be recovered.
Assume the local command also changed the remote and satisfied all hosting-platform policies.
questions.answer_key: Inspect the repository state, verify the expected result, and protect valuable work before destructive or history-changing operations.
questions.explanation: Inspect the repository state, verify the expected result, and protect valuable work before destructive or history-changing operations.
